articles.title: Defesa Civil confirma 2ª morte e 23 cidades de SC em emergência | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo óbito foi de mulher eletrocutada em Xanxerê, cidade onde tornado foi confirmado. Equipes seguem mobilizadas no atendimento às famílias e na distribuição de donativos.
articles.summary: Equipes seguem mobilizadas no atendimento às famílias e na distribuição de donativos.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil confirmou, nesta quinta-feira (5), que subiu para dois o número de mortos devido aos temporais em Santa Catarina . A segunda morte ocorreu em Xanxerê (SC), quando uma mulher de 46 anos foi eletrocutada ao encostar em um cabo de alta tensão, na quarta-feira (4) . O nome dela não foi revelado.

Até o momento, dois tornados foram confirmados no estado: em Chapecó e Xanxerê. A corporação agora investiga se o fenômeno também atingiu outros municípios, como Rio Negrinho , que registrou estragos e a primeira morte: a de um jovem de 20 anos atingido pela cobertura de um posto de combustíveis que desabou com a força do vento .

O número de municípios com decretos de emergência também subiu para 23 . Até o fim da noite de quarta, eram 20 cidades nessa situação. Veja o balanço dos estragos no estado :

23 municípios em situação de emergência;

5.358 residências danificadas ou afetadas;

252 pessoas desalojadas (em casas de parentes ou amigos);

56 pessoas desabrigadas (acolhidas em abrigos públicos).

Equipes da Defesa Civil, Corpo de Bombeiros e prefeituras seguem mobilizadas no atendimento às famílias, desobstrução de vias e distribuição de lonas e donativos nas regiões mais atingidas.

Em Chapecó, as aulas na rede municipal também foram suspensas. Houve danos em unidades de saúde, e nesta quinta somente o Centro de Saúde Seminário segue fechado. Outros seis apresentam problemas de energia elétrica ou conexão com a internet.

Tornado derrubou veículos em Xanxerê — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

Bombeiros foram chamados às 19h30 e encontraram a vítima sem sinais vitais, caída e em contato físico direto com a fiação energizada.

O local foi isolado e a empresa DCELT Energia, que fornece o serviço na cidade, foi acionada para desligar a energia do trecho. O g1 procurou a concessionária nesta manhã e aguardava retorno.

A primeira morte foi registrada na tarde de quarta, quando a cobertura que abrigava a aérea de abastecimento do posto, localizado na BR-280 no bairro Vila Nova, desabou. Jonathan Oliveira da Cruz foi atingido e não resistiu aos ferimentos.

"Jonathan fazia parte da nossa equipe e era querido por todos que conviviam com ele. Neste momento de dor, nos solidarizamos com seus familiares, amigos e colegas de trabalho, e estamos prestando todo o apoio e assistência necessários à família", disse o comunicado da Rede de Postos M7.

🎶🎭 Música, teatro, exposições, feiras e festas : a agenda cultural de novembro do g1 Santa Catarina está recheada de opções para todos os gostos e idades neste mês. Confira os destaques dos próximos dias e programe-se para aproveitar o melhor da cena cultural.

A segunda edição do Festival Latino-Americano de Cinema Ambiental (FLACA) apresenta 25 filmes - entre documentários, ficções e animações -produzidos no Brasil, Argentina, Bolívia, Colômbia, Cuba, Espanha, Polônia e Peru.

O evento ocorre entre os dias 31 de outubro e 7 novembro de 2026 na Sala de Cinema Gilberto Gerlach (CIC), em Florianópolis.

Além das produções, a programação gratuita inclui debates com realizadores e convidados, atividades formativas e um seminário dedicado às relações entre comunidades tradicionais e meio ambiente.

Festival gratuito de cinema vai exibir 25 filmes de oito países em Florianópolis — Foto: Divulgação

8 de novembro: Florianópolis - Final do concurso 'Santa Catarina Canta 2026'

No domingo (8), a partir das 17h, a Avenida Beira-Mar Continental recebe a grande final do Santa Catarina Canta.

A noite começa com os 21 finalistas das sete regiões do estado se apresentando ao lado da Camerata Florianópolis, sob regência do maestro Jeferson Della Rocca, disputando os primeiros lugares nas categorias Geral e Infantojuvenil.

A partir das 20h, haverá shows de Fernando e Sorocaba e Sérgio Reis. A entrada é gratuita.

Até 8 de novembro - Animaneco em Joinville , Jaraguá do Sul , São Francisco do Sul e Corupá

Considerado o maior festival de teatro de animação do Brasil, o 8º Animaneco – Festival Internacional de Teatro de Boneco reúne artistas de seis países ao longo de 11 dias. Os ingressos para as apresentações em espaços fechados são distribuídos gratuitamente e podem ser retirados pelo site, com limite de dois ingressos por CPF .

A programação inclui 14 espetáculos, 15 apresentações de teatro lambe-lambe e sete performances.

As atrações abrangem diferentes técnicas de teatro e animação, como marionetes, fantoches, teatro de sombras e manipulação de objetos. Participam artistas de diferentes estados brasileiros, além de representantes da Espanha, México, Argentina, Uruguai e Chile.

Entre os espaços que receberão as apresentações estão o Teatro Censupeg, o Teatro do Sesc, o Museu Nacional de Imigração e Colonização, o Teatro da Ajote, o CEU Aventureiro e o Museu de Arte de Joinville (MAJ).

No dia 13 de novembro de 2026, o Music Park BC, em Balneário Camboriú , recebe um encontro entre dois dos maiores nomes do reggae brasileiro: Armandinho e Vitor Kley. O público poderá reviver grandes sucessos, celebrar boas vibrações e cantar do início ao fim em um show repleto de energia, emoção e conexão.

Um olhar sobre memória, isolamento e apagamento histórico marca o Cine Garagem 2026, que apresentará quatro curtas-metragens catarinenses na Fundação Cultural Badesc, em Florianópolis. A entrada é gratuita.

As exibições serão realizadas em duas sessões gratuitas: na sexta-feira (13), às 19h, serão exibidos os quatro curtas-metragens, em uma sessão com acessibilidade em Libras e audiodescrição, seguida de debate com o curador e representantes dos filmes.

Em 21 de novembro, o artista retorna à Arena Opus, em São José, com a Emicida Racional MCMV Tour, na Arena Opus.

A apresentação traz ao palco o aclamado Emicida Racional VL 2 – Mesmas Cores & Mesmos Valores, de 2025, construído a partir da relação do artista com uma das maiores referências do rap nacional: os Racionais. A exposição “Da pele à terra: percursos de pousos e riscos”, de Damiana Bregalda, reúne obras que refletem sobre a relação entre o ser humano e a Terra, questionando formas de ocupação, domínio e exploração do território.

Com curadoria de Juliana Crispe, a mostra gratuita tem visitação gratuita até 29 de novembro de 2026, de terça a domingo, das 10h às 21h. Ela ocorre no Museu da Imagem e do Som de Santa Catarina (MIS/SC), no Centro Integrado de Cultura (CIC).

O conjunto é resultado de mais de dez anos de pesquisa artística e antropológica, realizada a partir de deslocamentos por diferentes territórios e de investigações sobre o corpo, a terra, o tempo e os modos de habitar o mundo.

articles.title: Campo Limpo Paulista recebe ajuda humanitária após enchentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Defesa civil, cerca de 200 famílias foram prejudicadas. Órgão deve mandar mais um carregamento de doações nesta quinta-feira (5).
articles.summary: Enchentes em Campo Limpo Paulista deixaram 200 famílias atingidas e 800 imóveis danificados; ajuda do Estado chega à cidade enquanto novos temporais são previstos.
articles.body:
Moradores de Campo Limpo Paulista (SP) receberam ajuda humanitária do governo estadual de São Paulo após os estragos das chuvas nesta terça-feira (3). Segundo a prefeitura, aproximadamente 200 famílias foram prejudicadas e 808 imóveis ficaram danificados.

A população que mora nos bairros São José e na comunidade Reviver receberam os kits de higiene pessoal e de limpeza para as casa, cobertores, cestas básica, água potável e lonas para proteção enviados pelo Fundo Social de São Paulo e Defesa Civil. A expectativa é que mais um carregamento de doações cheguem à cidade nesta quinta-feira (5).

Campo Limpo Paulista declarou estado de emergência após diferentes bairros sofrerem com uma enxurrada pelo transbordamento do Rio Jundiaí no último domingo (1º). De acordo com a Defesa Civil, o volume de chuva foi elevado para um período curto de tempo. Em cerca de 40 minutos, houve 40 milímetros de precipitação, conforme estimativa do órgão.

Um pedido de ajuda humanitária foi enviado para o estado e os kits começaram a chegar na cidade durante a semana.

Defesa Civil entregou kits de ajuda humanitária em Campo Limpo Paulista — Foto: Defesa Civil / Imagens cedidas

No levantamento da prefeitura, as regiões mais afetadas foram, principalmente, os bairros São José, Jardim Marchetti, Parque Internacional, Jardim Santiago e Santa Catarina.

Além do atendimento a população, servidores da Secretaria de Obras e Serviços Públicos têm trabalhado para o desassoreamento de córregos e rios. Equipes também estão mobilizadas para a limpeza da cidade e retirada da lama nas vias.

Defesa Civil de Campo Limpo Paulista (SP) estima que houve 40 milímetros de chuva em menos de uma hora, volume considerado elevado — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

A Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta para o risco de temporais em todo o estado de São Paulo (SP) até sábado (7). A previsão é de chuva forte, ventos de até 80 kmh/h e possibilidade de granizo.

A possibilidade das pancadas de chuva é maior para os períodos da madrugada e manhã. No domingo (8), deve haver queda de temperatura. Um Gabinete de Crise foi preparado para ficar de plantão a partir desta quinta-feira (5) em São Paulo.

O órgão reforça orientações preventivas para evitar acidentes durante o período de instabilidade:

Alagamentos: evite áreas inundadas e não tente atravessar vias com acúmulo de água, mesmo que a profundidade pareça pequena;

Ventos fortes: mantenha distância de árvores, postes, fiação elétrica e estruturas metálicas;

Encostas e morros: fique atento a sinais de deslizamento de terra e, diante de qualquer alteração, procure um local seguro;

Trânsito: motoristas devem reduzir a velocidade e aumentar a distância de segurança em relação aos demais veículos.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelo telefone 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo número 193. Para receber os alertas meteorológicos gratuitos via SMS no celular, basta enviar uma mensagem com o CEP da residência para o número 40199.

articles.title: Voo que ia a Roma faz pouso de emergência em base aérea francesa após ameaça de bomba | G1
articles.standfirst: Airbus 320 vinha de Dublin, na Irlanda, quando foi obrigado a desviar a rota. França acompanha caso, diz premiê Sébastien Lecornu. Incidente é o sétimo do tipo desde o início da semana na aviação comercial europeia.
articles.summary: Airbus 320 vinha de Dublin, na Irlanda, quando foi obrigado a desviar a rota. França acompanha caso, diz premiê Sébastien Lecornu. Incidente é o sétimo do tipo desde o início da semana na aviação comercial europeia.
articles.body:
Avião Airbus A320 da companhia aérea Aer Lingus após fazer pouso de emergência na base aérea de Évreux, no norte da França, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

Um voo que tinha como destino Roma , na Itália, fez um pouso de emergência na base aérea francesa de Évreux após um alerta de bomba, informou nesta quinta-feira (5) o gabinete do primeiro-ministro francês, Sébastien Lecornu.

O avião, um Airbus A320 da companhia aérea Aer Lingus, partiu de Dublin , na Irlanda, e declarou emergência a bordo quando estava sobrevoando a região norte do território francês.

A aeronave pousou na base aérea, todos os 151 passageiros e seis tripulantes foram evacuados com segurança e um esquadrão antibomba foi mobilizado para fazer uma inspeção na aeronave, segundo a França.

O incidente desta quinta ocorre após uma série de ameaças de bomba que provocaram transtornos em voos comerciais em toda a Europa nos últimos dias. Essas ameaças obrigaram mudanças de rota, pousos de emergência e varreduras de segurança.

Desde o início da semana, outros 15 incidentes desse tipo foram registrados, incluindo mais de 10 apenas nesta quinta-feira . Apesar dos alertas, nenhum explosivo foi encontrado até o momento.

Um voo comercial pode pousar em uma base aérea militar, porém geralmente se dá preferência a aeroportos civis, e essa opção é utilizada quando autoridades competentes autorizam ou quando a situação exige.

articles.title: Uelton de Souza Almeida: Por que o vereador preso mantém o mandato? | G1
articles.standfirst: Uelton de Souza Almeida pediu licença não remunerada da Câmara Municipal. Advogado explica quais situações podem levar à perda do mandato e diferencia a cadeira eletiva do cargo de secretário.
articles.summary: Uelton de Souza Almeida, suspeito de matar GCM, mantém cadeira na Câmara de Arujá via licença enquanto aguarda júri popular por homicídio qualificado.
articles.body:
Secretário adjunto de Segurança de Arujá é investigado por homicídio — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Social

O ex-secretário adjunto de Segurança de Arujá , Uelton de Souza Almeida, suspeito de matar o Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM) Nelson Caetano de Lima Neto, segue como vereador na cidade mesmo após ser preso. Segundo a Câmara Municipal da cidade, o vereador está apenas afastado do cargo.

➡️ Uelton se entregou à polícia em 26 de dezembro de 2025. Ele foi exonerado do cargo de secretário adjunto e suspenso das funções de GCM, seu cargo de origem. Em 22 de janeiro de 2026, a Justiça converteu a prisão temporária em preventiva.

Apesar disso, o ex-secretário continuava com mandato de vereador ativo na câmara municipal da cidade . Em 23 de fevereiro de 2026, ele pediu um afastamento não remunerado para tratar de interesses particulares , segundo a Câmara Municipal.

A licença o afastou temporariamente do mandato, mas não significou a perda da cadeira. De acordo com Luiz David Costa Faria, advogado e membro da Comissão de Direito Eleitoral da OAB-SP, a prisão não equivale a uma condenação definitiva nem encerra automaticamente o mandato.

“A Constituição presume a inocência até o trânsito em julgado”, afirmou. O advogado acrescentou que, apesar disso, uma condenação criminal definitiva pode sim levar à suspensão dos direitos políticos.

O julgamento de Uelton está marcado para 15 de dezembro de 2026, às 9h, no Plenário do Júri do Fórum de Arujá.

Em 23 de fevereiro de 2026, Uelton pediu licença não remunerada do mandato por 180 dias, para tratar de interesses particulares. O pedido foi feito com base no inciso IV do artigo 76 do Regimento Interno da Câmara.

Betinho, primeiro suplente, assumiu a vaga. Depois que ele também se licenciou para voltar à Secretaria Municipal de Esportes, Moisés Chocolate, segundo suplente, tomou posse, em 2 de março.

Com o fim do período inicial de 180 dias, em agosto, o vereador pediu uma extensão da licença, de mais 180 dias.

Segundo o advogado, a análise deve considerar a frequência, as justificativas apresentadas e o direito de defesa. A prisão, por si só, não justifica automaticamente todas as faltas.

A Lei Orgânica de Arujá e o Decreto-Lei nº 201/1967 preveem consequências para vereadores que deixam de comparecer a pelo menos um terço das sessões ordinárias de cada sessão legislativa, ressalvadas as hipóteses previstas em lei.

Segundo o advogado, a análise deve considerar a frequência, as justificativas e o direito de defesa. A prisão, por si só, não é uma justificativa automática para todas as faltas.

A Lei Orgânica também prevê a perda do mandato em situações como condenação criminal definitiva, perda ou suspensão dos direitos políticos e infração ao decoro parlamentar. O Decreto-Lei nº 201/1967 prevê a cassação pela Câmara em casos de conduta incompatível com a dignidade da Casa ou falta de decoro.

Nos casos de cassação por falta de decoro, a legislação prevê um processo com ampla defesa. A prisão ou a suspeita de um crime, por si só, não provocam a perda automática do mandato.

A exoneração da Prefeitura afeta o mandato?

Não. Segundo o advogado, a exoneração encerrou a nomeação de Uelton como secretário adjunto. O mandato de vereador é eletivo; não se trata de um cargo comissionado que possa ser exonerado.

O mandato pode terminar por renúncia, pelo fim do período para o qual o vereador foi eleito ou por uma das hipóteses previstas em lei, conforme o procedimento aplicável.

Se for absolvido, ele pode voltar ao cargo na Prefeitura?

Sim. O prefeito pode nomear Uelton novamente para o cargo de secretário adjunto, caso tenha interesse e os requisitos legais sejam atendidos. A absolvição, por si só, não garante a renomeação.

A situação de Uelton como guarda civil municipal é diferente. Como ele também foi suspenso dessa função, um eventual retorno depende das regras administrativas do município e do motivo da suspensão.

Uelton é suspeito de atirar 12 vezes no GCM de Mogi das Cruzes, Nelson Caetano de Lima Neto. O crime aconteceu na noite do dia 24 de dezembro de 2025, na casa onde a atual namorada de Nelson, que era ex-esposa de Uelton, morava em Arujá.

Segundo o pai da vítima, na noite do crime, a namorada de Nelson o convidou para um churrasco na casa onde ela morava com o ex-marido. Em mensagens trocadas por celular, o GCM avisou que estava a caminho e levando carne para o evento.

Embora separados há cinco anos, a mulher e Uelton dividiam o mesmo imóvel. Ele morava na parte superior e ela na inferior.

A namorada, então, teria pedido para ele esperar um pouco, pois o ex-marido ainda estava no local. Pouco depois, ela teria dito que ele já poderia ir, pois o ex-marido havia saído.

Contudo, quando Nelson chegou, o suspeito ainda estava na casa e, segundo a família, atirou 12 vezes contra ele. "O cara estava lá e deu 12 tiros nele", relatou o pai.

articles.title: Quem é Santiago Peña? Presidente de direita do Paraguai renunciou ao cargo em meio a crise bancária | G1
articles.standfirst: Aliado de Trump, Peña foi pai aos 17, estudou economia em Assunção, fez pós nos EUA, trabalhou no FMI e no Banco Central do Paraguai e foi ministro da Fazenda.
articles.summary: Aliado de Trump, Peña foi pai aos 17, estudou economia em Assunção, fez pós nos EUA, trabalhou no FMI e no Banco Central do Paraguai e foi ministro da Fazenda.
articles.body:
O presidente eleito do Paraguai, Santiago Peña (à esquerda), e o vice Pedro Alliana, concedem entrevista após reunião com Lula no Palácio do Planalto — Foto: Pedro Henrique Gomes/g1

O presidente do Paraguai , Santiago Peña, renunciou ao cargo nesta quinta-feira (5), em meio a uma crise política. Mais cedo, o Congresso do país havia tomado os primeiros passos para votar um impeachment contra Peña e seu vice.

➡️ A crise começou após o banco digital Ueno fechar as portas e deixar milhares de clientes sem acesso ao próprio dinheiro. Peña foi acionista do grupo que controla a instituição, e a oposição acusa o Banco Central paraguaio de encobrir irregularidades.

Santiago Peña, de 47 anos, foi eleito presidente em abril de 2023. Filiado ao Partido Colorado, de direita, ele substituiu Mario Abdo Benítez na Presidência do Paraguai, que também pertence ao mesmo partido.

Em 2023 foi a segunda vez que ele candidatou: em 2018, Peña perdeu as primárias do Partido Colorado para o antecessor, Mario Abdo Benítez.

Peña foi pai adolescente, ele teve um filho aos 17 anos, quando ainda estava na escola. Ele ainda é casado com Leticia Ocampo, com quem teve um outro filho.

Santiago Peña é economista com formação nos Estados Unidos e uma passagem pelo Fundo Monetário Internacional —ele foi trabalhar no FMI aos 30 anos.

Ele foi ministro da Fazenda do Paraguai durante o governo de Horácio Cartes (2013 a 2018) e, durante seu tempo no ministério, filiou-se ao Partido Colorado, o mais tradicional do Paraguai.

Ele é graduado pela Universidad Católica Nuestra Señora de Asunción, do Paraguai, e conseguiu um trabalho no Banco Central do país. Depois disso, foi fazer uma pós na universidade de Columbia, nos EUA, e então arrumou um emprego no FMI. Ele trabalhou no departamento do FMI para a África.

Depois de voltar do trabalho no FMI, ele incialmente voltou Banco Central do Paraguai. Depois, entre 2015 e 2017, tornou-se ministro da Fazenda do país e, quando acabou o governo de Cartes, ele foi trabalhar no banco do antigo chefe.

Santiago é de direita, ele pertence ao Partido Colorado, que domina a política paraguaia desde a década de 1950

O economista foi eleito em 2023, quando derrotou Efraín Alegre. Na época, acreditava-se que a popularidade do partido do vencedor estaria em baixa por uma economia em desaceleração e acusações de corrupção.

articles.title: Doação de órgãos de passageiro morto em Teresina ajuda 5 pessoas | G1
articles.standfirst: Edilson Lima, de 49 anos, ficou gravamente ferido em um acidente no último dia 29 de outubro, em Teresina, e faleceu na quarta-feira (4).
articles.summary: A doação de órgãos do passageiro Edilson Lima, vítima de acidente em Teresina, beneficiou pacientes em Pernambuco, São Paulo, Brasília e no Piauí.
articles.body:
A família de Edilson Lima, passageiro de 49 anos que morreu após estrutura com bandeira do Piauí atingir um ônibus no dia 29 de outubro, em Teresina, autorizou a doação de órgãos da vítima. No total, cinco pessoas foram beneficiadas com a doação.

A retirada de rins, fígado, córneas e fígado ocorreram na manhã desta quinta-feira (5), no Hospital de Urgência de Teresina, onde Edilson ficou internado por seis dias após sofrer o acidente.

De acordo com a coordenadora da Comissão Intra-Hospitalar de Doação de Órgãos do HUT, Milena Cantuária, os rins foram destinados a pacientes dos estados de Pernambuco e São Paulo. Já o fígado irá ser transplantado para uma pessoa de Brasília, enquanto as córneas ajudarão pacientes do Piauí.

Paulo Natanael detalhou ao g1 que a iniciativa partiu da família, pois o assunto não chegou a ser discutido com o pai.

"Ele não comentou sobre isso, mas, pela personalidade dele e tendo em vista que, mesmo após sua partida, ele poderia ajudar na vida de outras pessoas, decidimos fazer a doação", afirmou o filho do doador.

Órgãos de passageiro que morreu após ônibus ser atingido por estrutura de bandeira são doados e beneficiam 5 pessoas — Foto: Reprodução (Redes sociais/Arquivo pessoal)

Edilson faleceu na quarta-feira (4), por traumatismo craniano, após seis dias internado em estado grave no HUT. Ele era passageiro do ônibus que foi atingido por uma estrutura de bandeira na Ponte Juscelino Kubitschek, na Avenida Frei Serafim, em Teresina. Na ocasião, ele e uma mulher foram socorridos inconscientes.

Segundo o filho da vítima, Edilson trabalhava como autônomo em Teresina e era bastante querido no meio familiar. Ele será sepultado em Castelo do Piauí, onde a maioria dos parentes vivem.

"Era uma pessoa muito preocupada com a família, disponível sempre em ajudar. Ele quem acompanhava a família de Castelo quando vinham para Teresina fazer exames, consultas. Ele tomava a frente de resolver essas questões", contou Paulo Natanael.

"Gostava muito de cozinhar. Quando chegava na casa da mãe dele ele gostava muito de fazer a comida. Quando ia pra minha casa também. Era um pai que gostava muito de me agradar", completou Paulo.

*Eduarda Barradas, estagiária sob supervisão de Lucas Marreiros.

articles.title: VÍDEO mostra avião na pista em passagem de tornado por Chapecó | G1
articles.standfirst: Áudio captou relato da tripulação da Azul, ainda na pista do Aeroporto de Chapecó, no momento da tempestade. Terminal teve equipamentos destruídos e operações seguem suspensas.
articles.summary: Áudio captou relato da tripulação da Azul no momento da tempestade; terminal teve equipamentos destruídos e operações seguem suspensas.
articles.body:
Um vídeo registrou o momento em que um avião da Azul Linhas Aéreas se preparava para decolar no Aeroporto de Chapecó , no Oeste de Santa Catarina , quando rajadas fortes de vento impediram o início do voo. A situação foi registrada na quarta-feira (4), dia em que a cidade foi atingida por um tornado.

A gravação também captou o áudio da tripulação na cabine ( assista acima ).

"Só avisando, nós estamos sobre a pista", diz um funcionário em um trecho. Logo depois, ele completa: "Só para vocês terem uma ideia, a gente está parado [inaudível], está chacoalhando muito".

Além de Chapecó, a cidade vizinha Xanxerê (SC) também confirmou a passagem de um tornado na quarta. Duas mortes já foram registradas no estado por causa das tempestades .

O vídeo foi cedido ao g1 pelo Portal Chapecó. Questionada sobre as imagens, a Azul informou que divulgará apenas dados operacionais. Em nota, a companhia comunicou o cancelamento de três voos: AD4274 e AD2983 (entre Chapecó e Campinas (SP) e AD4348 (de Chapecó para Florianópolis ) ( íntegra no fim do texto ).

A concessionária Voe Xap, que administra o terminal, também não comentou as imagens. Informou apenas que pousos e decolagens continuam suspensos e que a tempestade causou estragos graves no terminal de passageiros e em equipamentos de solo.

Tornado atinge aeroporto de Chapecó, no Oeste de Santa Catarina — Foto: Portal Chapecó/Imagem cedida

A paranaense Andrea Cristina Viganó estava dentro do avião. Ela relatou ao g1 PR que a aeronave chegou a ser arrastada pelo vento. Quando conseguiu desembarcar, encontrou parte da estrutura do aeroporto destruída.

"Foi uma coisa muito estranha, porque nós entramos no avião e saímos de um aeroporto perfeito. [...] Dentro da tempestade, nós passamos uns dez minutos e, quando nós saímos disso, não existia mais aeroporto", contou.

Andrea é de Pato Branco, no sudoeste do Paraná, e estava acompanhada da mãe, Celis Mara Viganó. As duas trabalham juntas em uma escola de inglês e viajariam para Campinas (SP), onde participariam de uma convenção da rede.

Tornado foi confirmado em Chapecó nesta quarta-feira (4) — Foto: Felipe Gomes/Divulgação

Frente do aeroporto de Chapecó ficou destruído por causa do temporal — Foto: NSC TV/Reprodução

A Azul informa que, devido ao fechamento por tempo indeterminado do aeroporto de Chapecó (SC), fato alheio ao controle da Companhia, os voos AD4274 e AD2983 (ambos Chapecó-Viracopos) e AD4348 (Chapecó-Florianópolis) desta quarta-feira, 04, precisaram ser cancelados.

A Azul lamenta os impactos causados pela forte tempestade que atingiu a cidade, e está prestando assistência aos Clientes e Tripulantes afetados, conforme previsto na Resolução nº 400/2016 (alterada pela Resolução nº 813) da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac). Os passageiros serão reacomodados em outros voos da Companhia, após o retorno das operações no local.

A Azul orienta que os Clientes com viagem nos próximos dias com embarque ou destino a Chapecó fiquem atentos às notificações e comunicados enviados por e-mail e aplicativo da empresa.

A Voe Xap, concessionária do Aeroporto de Chapecó, informa que as operações permanecem suspensas temporariamente em razão da forte tempestade que atingiu a cidade na manhã da última quarta-feira (4 de novembro).

Desde então, equipes técnicas da concessionária avançam nos trabalhos de limpeza e recuperação das áreas afetadas, incluindo o terminal de passageiros, o restabelecimento das duas estações meteorológicas (EMS), que também deverão passar por nova homologação pelas autoridades competentes, e a recomposição da cerca operacional. Todas as ações estão concentradas em garantir a retomada segura das operações no menor prazo possível.

A tempestade também provocou danos significativos a equipamentos utilizados pelas empresas de serviços de solo, como escadas, tratores e carrinhos de bagagem. A Voe Xap segue prestando apoio a essas empresas na recuperação dos equipamentos, essenciais para as operações da aviação comercial.

Lamentamos eventuais transtornos e orientamos que os passageiros não se dirijam ao aeroporto neste momento. Para informações sobre remarcações de passagens, a recomendação é entrar em contato diretamente com as companhias aéreas.

articles.title: Atendimento no Tesourinho em Taubaté tem filas por falha no sistema | G1
articles.standfirst: Instabilidade ocorre após troca de sistema interno de gestão da administração municipal; prefeitura afirma que alguns serviços já foram normalizados e outros estão em processo de correção.
articles.summary: O atendimento no Tesourinho, em Taubaté, registra filas e demora nesta quinta-feira após a prefeitura substituir o sistema interno de gestão durante o feriado.
articles.body:
Fila de moradores no préd Tesourinho em Taubaté. — Foto: Laurene Santos/Rede Vanguarda

Moradores que procuram atendimento no prédio do Tesourinho, no Centro de Taubaté (SP), enfrentam filas e demora nesta quinta-feira (5).

O local concentra diferentes serviços da Prefeitura, entre eles atendimentos relacionados ao cadastro imobiliário e ao Imposto Predial e Territorial Urbano (IPTU).

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Taubaté informou que a lentidão está relacionada à instabilidade em um sistema interno de gestão, que foi substituído nos últimos dias, durante o feriado.

Segundo a administração municipal, a nova plataforma vai substituir diferentes sistemas utilizados pelos órgãos da prefeitura, que não operavam de forma totalmente integrada e alguns já estavam tecnologicamente defasados.

A prefeitura explicou que a transição envolveu um grande volume de dados e etapas de transferência, importação e validação de informações. Com isso, alguns serviços apresentaram instabilidade.

Ainda de acordo com a administração municipal, parte dos problemas já foi corrigida, enquanto outros seguem em processo de regularização.

Prédio do Tesourinho, no Centro de Taubaté, onde moradores enfrentam filas e demora no atendimento após instabilidade em sistema da Prefeitura. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Segundo apuração da repórter Laurene Santos, da Rede Vanguarda , a Prefeitura confirmou que está mantido para o próximo sábado um mutirão de atendimento para esclarecer dúvidas sobre o programa de anistia de multas e juros.

O atendimento será realizado das 8h às 13h e será exclusivo para tratar do programa. Os interessados podem fazer a inscrição pela internet ou comparecer diretamente ao local durante o mutirão.

articles.title: Suffolk tractor parade says Facebook slow to deal with fake pages
articles.summary: An annual Christmas charity tractor run says Facebook's owner Meta takes too long to address scams.
articles.body:
A charity event organiser says Facebook needs to do more to protect its supporters from fake online profiles that have been set up for a third year running.

The Suffolk Tractor Light Parade will see about 200 vehicles travel around the east of the county on 13 December.

As in 2024 and 2025, Facebook pages posing as the official event were set up, and the genuine organisers feared supporters could be asked to donate to scam accounts.

Organiser Liz Quickenden said she had repeatedly reported the issue to Facebook owner Meta, but had been told its guidelines had not been violated. After being contacted by the BBC Meta acknowledged the pages had violated policies and removed them.

"It has taken the BBC to approach them for them to do anything about it, and that says everything - so they absolutely need to do more," said Quickenden.

"Trying to speak to a human is impossible, so it's really hard to get these things taken down; it's exhausting; I'm lost as to what we can do."

According to Meta's Community Standards pages on its website, content on its platform must be authentic and "we don't want people using our services to misrepresent who they are or what they're doing".

Quickenden said those behind the fake accounts – be it humans or bots – were using the event's imagery and wording, yet she had still received "no support" from Meta.

"It's infuriating because we're just trying to do something good, but we have no idea who these people are," she added.

The parade was started as a "very small event with just 30 tractors" after the Covid-19 pandemic as a way to raise money for local charities.

The ride-out starts and ends in Campsea Ashe and takes in Woodbridge, Rendlesham and Wickham Market.

Now in its fifth year, the event has raised more than £45,000.

The good causes due to benefit from this year's event will be Brave Futures, Home Start Suffolk, and YANA: You Are Not Alone.

However, Quickenden worries its always-generous supporters may start to feel more reluctant to donate or get involved out of fear of being scammed.

The fake Facebook accounts are not believed to have directly contacted anyone yet this year, but in the past tractor owners have asked to transfer money into a bank up front to take part.

Quickenden said supporters who had inadvertently followed fake accounts had been messaged in previous years. She emphasised that donations could only be made through the event's official website .

"It just makes everything a little bit more stressful, but this is about us being proactive rather than reactive," said Quickenden.

"I obviously can't swear, but what I would like to say is probably not publishable."

Meta told the BBC it was always developing new ways to make it harder for scammers to operate on its platforms.

It said that last year it said it took down more than 159 million scam ads, with more than 92% detected proactively before anyone reported them, and also removed 10.9 million accounts associated with criminal scam centres.

articles.title: Indiana executes man convicted of killing 2 children as 2 more US executions loom Thursday
articles.summary: Three executions are scheduled across Indiana, Florida and Alabama in the second instance this year of three people facing the death penalty on the same day.
articles.body: Indiana executed a man convicted of killing his girlfriend's two young children early Thursday, marking the first of three executions scheduled across the U.S. on the same day. Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, was pronounced dead at 12:45 a.m. at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City after receiving a lethal injection, according to the Indiana Department of Correction. Florida and Alabama are set to carry out executions later Thursday, which would mark the second time this year that three death row inmates have been put to death on the same day. The first such day this year took place on August 13, when Oklahoma, Tennessee and Alabama executed three inmates within hours of each other. FLORIDA PUTS 77-YEAR-OLD MAN TO DEATH FOR DEPUTY'S MURDER AS STATE CLOSES IN ON EXECUTION RECORD In Florida, Thursday's execution would be the state's 19th of 2026, matching the record set last year. Alabama is preparing for its third execution of the year, while Indiana has now carried out its first. Jesse Guardado, 64, is scheduled to be executed in Florida after confessing and pleading guilty to fatally stabbing a 75-year-old woman who had helped him find a job and housing in 2004. Guardado killed Jackie Malone inside her home before stealing her jewelry box, $80 and other items to fund his drug addiction. "Jesse Guardado has accepted responsibility for killing Jackie Malone and has consistently expressed deep remorse. Florida should accept responsibility for what it did to him as a child, too," Grace Hanna, executive director of Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty, said in a statement while urging the state to halt the execution. Florida has ramped up executions as Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis has signed a series of death warrants since 2025. The state carried out a record 19 executions last year, more than under any other Florida governor in a single year since the death penalty was reinstated in 1976. Those executions accounted for roughly 40% of the 47 carried out nationwide in 2025. Florida has also accounted for more than half of the 32 executions carried out nationwide before Thursday's scheduled executions. In July, Florida executed two prisoners on the same day, marking the first double execution by a single state in nearly a decade. In Alabama, Michael Taylor, 54, is scheduled to be executed for the 1991 murders of an older couple who were beaten to death with a metal bar during a robbery inside their home. Authorities caught Taylor in Birmingham, about an hour away, with the victims' Cadillac. Alabama officials plan to execute Taylor by lethal injection after a judge ruled against his attorneys' objections to the method. Taylor had previously requested execution by nitrogen gas, and his attorneys sought to preserve that choice. ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION Death penalty opponents urged Republican Gov. Kay Ivey to commute Taylor's sentence to life in prison, arguing that he was too young and immature at 19 to fully appreciate the consequences of his actions. "If the state kills Michael, it is not the 19-year-old who made the worst mistake of his life who it kills. But the mature, well-respected, God-fearing man sitting in that cell today," Esther Brown of Project Hope to Abolish the Death Penalty told The Associated Press. Ivey rejected the clemency requests, clearing the way for Taylor's scheduled execution. In Indiana, Weisheit was executed for setting a 2010 house fire that killed his girlfriend's two children, ages 8 and 5, as the couple's relationship deteriorated. The lethal injection began shortly after midnight, and Weisheit was pronounced dead at 12:45 a.m., according to Noelle Russell, chief communications officer for the Indiana Department of Correction. Weisheit requested barbecue ribs for his final meal and did not make a final statement, Russell said. His attorneys sought permission for additional brain scans, arguing that his history of head injuries and mental health problems warranted further examination. Republican Gov. Mike Braun denied the request. Braun also rejected appeals to commute Weisheit's death sentence to life in prison. FLORIDA EXECUTES INMATE WHO KILLED CELLMATE BECAUSE HE WANTED DEATH PENALTY Weisheit's lawyers had also raised separate concerns about Indiana's planned use of execution drugs obtained from a pharmacy facing a disciplinary hearing before the Indiana Pharmacy Board next week. The Indiana Department of Correction, however, maintained that it was confident in its ability to carry out the execution humanely. Following the execution, Braun said Weisheit's case had undergone repeated reviews in state and federal courts. "These reviews have never resulted in an overturned sentence," Braun said in a statement. "Today, Weisheit's sentence has been carried out as ordered by the court." Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita also weighed in, saying the execution delivered "long-awaited justice for Alyssa Lynch and her brother Caleb, two innocent children whose lives were stolen in an act of unspeakable cruelty." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The planned executions come amid renewed scrutiny of lethal injection procedures following a failed execution attempt in Tennessee in September. Death row inmate Christa Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital and was rushed to a hospital. She has since returned to prison. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Russia says Ukrainian postal hub, ship hit; Kyiv strikes Ryazan refinery
articles.summary: Injuries reported on both sides as Russia and Ukraine trade overnight drone strikes on energy and logistics sites.
articles.body:
Russia and Ukraine have traded drone attacks on each other’s infrastructure, causing injuries on both sides.

Moscow said on Thursday that it struck a postal logistics hub, a power substation and a cargo ship, while Ukrainian drones set off fires in an industrial zone in the Russian city of Ryazan, about 200km (125 miles) southeast of the capital.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Telegram that its forces had used drones to hit a terminal of Nova Poshta, Ukraine’s largest private delivery company, in the village of Novyi Korotych outside Kharkiv. It said it also struck a 330-kilovolt substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region and a dry cargo ship carrying military equipment in the Black Sea, 52km (32 miles) southwest of the port of Odesa.

Ukrainian officials did not immediately confirm the strikes on the postal terminal or the vessel.

Kharkiv Governor Oleh Syniehubov said Russia had attacked the city and 17 settlements in the region over the past day with more than 80 drones, injuring six people, including a child.

In the eastern Donetsk region, Governor Vadym Filashkin said Russian attacks killed four civilians and injured five others on Wednesday, with two people killed in Serhiivka and two in Yasnohirka. Local outlet Novosti Donbasu reported that the two killed in Yasnohirka were women who died when Russian forces struck the village with two glide bombs.

Moscow says the logistics sites it targets serve the Ukrainian military. Nova Poshta facilities have been hit repeatedly, including in an attack on a sorting centre in Kyiv in August that killed three people.

Russian drones also caused large fires in the Bucha district outside Kyiv overnight. A logistics centre was targeted there, and one person was injured.

Meanwhile in Russia, Ryazan Governor Pavel Malkov said more than 200 Ukrainian drones had attacked the region overnight.

He said falling debris caused fires at several industrial sites and damaged power lines, cutting electricity to parts of the city, and one person was injured. Malkov later said power had been restored and the fires had been extinguished or contained.

Malkov did not name the sites that were hit. However, footage verified by the independent Russian outlet Astra showed a fire at the Ryazan oil refinery, which is owned by state energy company Rosneft and is among Russia’s largest.

“It’s evident that Ukraine has intensified its strikes on Russian oil refineries” after a brief pause in late October, said Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow.

She noted that the Yaroslavl refinery had been attacked just two days earlier. Windows were also shattered at a school in Ryazan and classes were cancelled.

Shapovalova said the strikes had not stopped Russian fuel production, but that shortages were occasionally reported “as people rush to gas stations to fill up their cars after the news about attacks on oil refineries”.

Russia, meanwhile, has intensified attacks on Ukraine’s power grid, causing rolling blackouts in Kyiv since mid-October.

“Some people here have not had things like electricity and, more importantly, water for days now,” Al Jazeera’s Audrey McAlpine said, reporting from Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv. “They would say that they can do without electricity, but water is another thing entirely.”

McAlpine said city authorities had indicated that heating would not be switched on until temperatures had stayed at minus 5 degrees Celsius for five consecutive days. As temperatures approach zero, she said, the outages become “a matter of life and death”.

articles.title: Donald Trump's Midas curse: Why his golden picks turned blue in US midterms 2026
articles.summary: Donald Trump wanted the 2026 midterms to be a referendum on his presidency and American voters obliged, delivering a verdict that could hardly have been
articles.body: Donald Trump wanted the 2026 midterms to be a referendum on his presidency and American voters obliged, delivering a verdict that could hardly have been more uncomfortable for him.The president had made himself the central protagonist of the election cycle. He endorsed hundreds of candidates, intervened in Republican primaries, headlined rallies and urged supporters to treat the midterms as an extension of his 2024 mandate. His gave a direct message that a vote for Republicans was a vote for Trump.But when the wider electorate had its say, Democrats captured both chambers of Congress, flipping seven Senate seats and winning a string of House races in traditionally Republican territory.Distancing himself, Trump wrote on Truth Social: "I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!"The midterm results have also exposed an uncomfortable paradox for the US president. Trump has rarely been more successful at getting his preferred candidates through Republican primaries. Yet his endorsement has proved considerably less reliable when those candidates face the general electorate.A look at the numbers tells a story of a politician whose influence within his party has grown, even as his ability to deliver victories beyond it appears to be weakening.The midterm scorecard: 2018, 2022 and 2026According to Ballotpedia's endorsement tracker, Trump endorsed 99 candidates in the 2018 midterms, 276 in 2022 and 351 in 2026. His expanding reach has been accompanied by greater success in Republican primaries, but a less consistent record in general elections.In 2018, his first midterm as president, Trump endorsed 37 candidates in primaries, of whom 95% won. His general-election record was considerably weaker as 56 of the 95 candidates he backed won, giving him a success rate of 59%.Four years later, his primary success rate dipped marginally to 93%, with 224 of 241 endorsees winning their nominations. But his general-election performance improved sharply. Of the 254 candidates he endorsed, 84% won.In 2026, the pattern has shifted again. His primary success rate climbed to 96%, with 302 of 315 candidates winning. But his general-election success rate fell to 70%, according to Ballotpedia's latest tracker.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The comparison reveals two distinct trends. His general-election record, however, has fluctuated sharply, from 59% in 2018 to 84% in 2022, before falling to around 70% in 2026.The numbers suggest that Trump's endorsement has become increasingly influential in deciding who represents the Republican Party, but that influence does not translate as consistently when candidates face the wider electorate.The Senate setbacksThe most consequential defeats came in Senate races, where Democrats flipped seven Republican-held seats to take control of the chamber. Several of the losses involved candidates Trump had backed or helped elevate.Texas: Trump backed Attorney General Ken Paxton over incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary. Paxton secured the nomination, but Democrat James Talarico defeated him in the general election. Texas had not elected a Democratic senator since 1988, making the result a major breach in Republican territory.Kansas: Republican Senator Roger Marshall lost to Democrat Adam Hamilton, ending a nearly century-long Republican hold on the Senate seat.North Carolina: Trump's preferred candidate, former Republican National Committee chairman Michael Whatley, lost to former Democratic governor Roy Cooper.South Carolina: Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Trump-backed Darline Graham in a state that had not elected a Democratic senator since 1998.Maine: Democrat Troy Jackson defeated incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins, ending her three-decade tenure in the chamber.Iowa: Democrat Josh Turek defeated Republican Ashley Hinson in another major setback for a party that had carried the state comfortably in the 2024 presidential election.Ohio: Democrat Sherrod Brown defeated Republican Jon Husted in a special Senate election, flipping another Republican-held seat.These defeats were significant not simply because of the candidates involved, but because of the political geography. Democrats made gains in states that Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, demonstrating how sharply the electoral mood had shifted.Texas offered perhaps the clearest illustration of the risks of Trump's intervention. By backing Paxton against Cornyn, Trump helped determine who carried the Republican banner into November. But winning the party nomination proved no guarantee of winning over the state.It would be impossible to establish that Cornyn would necessarily have won. Yet the result has given Republicans another reason to examine whether loyalty to Trump is becoming a substitute for an electoral appeal.The kingmaker's changing roleThe comparison with 2022 is particularly revealing because Trump was operating from a very different political position.In 2022, he was a former president trying to retain his grip on the Republican Party while Joe Biden occupied the White House. His endorsements often targeted Republicans who had crossed him, particularly those who had rejected his claims about the 2020 election.Georgia offered a prominent example. Governor Brian Kemp and Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger, both of whom had resisted Trump's pressure over the 2020 results, defeated Trump-backed primary challengers.By 2026, Trump was no longer an outsider trying to shape the party from Mar-a-Lago. He was the incumbent president, with considerably greater influence over Republican candidate selection.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();That change was reflected in the primary numbers. His success rate rose from 93% to 96%, suggesting that his hold over the party's nomination process had strengthened.But being the incumbent also changed the stakes of the general election. Republican candidates were no longer simply campaigning against an unpopular Democratic administration. They were defending Trump's governing record.The president's political brand had become both their biggest asset in Republican primaries and a potential liability in the wider election.The primary victory trapThe results point to a structural problem in Trump's candidate-selection strategy, as a candidate who appeals strongly to Republican primary voters may not necessarily appeal to independents and moderate voters in a general election.Republican primaries are decided by a more ideologically concentrated electorate, in which Trump's endorsement carries considerable weight. General elections involve a broader coalition, including voters who may support Republican policies but have reservations about the president.Texas showed that tension. Trump's backing helped Paxton secure the nomination over Cornyn, but the former attorney general subsequently lost to Talarico.There may be a longer-term organisational problem for Republicans, too. Trump's influence over primaries has increasingly made loyalty to the president an important qualification for political survival within the party.That may be an effective way of enforcing discipline, but it also narrows the party's candidate pool. Republicans who might appeal to independents or moderate voters can find themselves vulnerable to primary challenges, while candidates with stronger ideological credentials emerge to represent the party in competitive states.From offence to defenceThere was also a fundamental difference in the political environment of the midterms in 2022 and 2026.In 2022, Trump could campaign against Biden and exploit dissatisfaction with the Democratic administration. In 2026, he was the president, and Republican candidates were effectively defending his record.Inflation, tariffs, the cost of living and the war with Iran became part of the electoral conversation. These were no longer abstract policy debates. They were questions about household budgets, fuel prices and whether voters felt better off under the administration.The AP Voter Poll, based on roughly 100,000 voters, found that around two-thirds blamed Trump's policies for fuelling inflation. About nine in 10 said the cost of living was a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress. Around six in 10 of these voters backed Democratic candidates in their local House races.The Iran war added another complication. The conflict, launched in February, pushed up energy costs, giving Democrats another line of attack against an administration already struggling to convince voters that their financial situation was improving.The poll also found that around seven in 10 voters believed the economy favoured the wealthy, while about six in 10 felt Trump's priorities were misplaced.The message was difficult for Republicans to escape. Their candidates were not merely fighting individual opponents; they were defending an administration that a sizeable section of the electorate believed was failing to address its everyday concerns.Backlash beyond CongressThe Democratic gains were not confined to Capitol Hill. The party also made significant advances in gubernatorial races, flipping Republican-held governorships in states including Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Nevada and Texas.The Texas result was particularly striking. Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, breaking a Republican hold on the governor's office that stretched back decades.In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson, while Ohio saw Democrat Amy Acton defeat Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.These victories suggest that the midterm backlash was not simply about individual congressional candidates or a handful of Senate contests. It extended to state-level politics, where Republicans had enjoyed considerable advantages.Democrats also gained ground in state legislatures, further weakening Republican dominance in several traditionally conservative states.For Trump, the implications extend beyond the immediate loss of congressional control. A Democratic majority in both chambers will make it considerably harder for the president to push his legislative agenda through Congress, while Democratic governors and state lawmakers will have greater influence over policy battles ahead of 2028.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2022, a 191-acre Indiana land listing triggered a much bigger conservation effort; 3,950 acres of former coal-mining land are now protected for wildlife and public access, a new account of the project reveals
articles.summary: What began as an attempt to save a 191-acre piece of land from a potential sale has grown into one of southern Indiana's significant conservation efforts.
articles.body: What began as an attempt to save a 191-acre piece of land from a potential sale has grown into one of southern Indiana's significant conservation efforts. Nearly 4,000 acres in Sullivan County are now permanently protected as the Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area, preserving wetlands, forests and former coal-mining land for wildlife and public recreation. A November 2 account by the Conservation Law Center, alongside reports from Indiana Public Media and The Indianapolis Star, has shed more light on how an unexpected property listing in 2022 set the larger project in motion. The conservation effort began when the Conservation Law Center's Southern Indiana Sentinel Landscape team noticed a 191-acre parcel listed on the open market in late 2022. The property was part of a much larger holding of nearly 4,000 acres owned by American Land Holdings of Indiana, a subsidiary of Peabody Energy.The land had a complicated history. Much of it had previously been part of the Minnehaha Fish and Wildlife Area, which closed in 2016 after the former landowner declined to renew its lease. The landscape, which includes reclaimed surface-mining ground, had gradually developed into a mix of bottomland forests, marshes, wetlands and upland grasslands. Conservationists feared that selling individual parcels could divide the connected landscape, potentially affecting wildlife habitats and the wetlands that help manage floodwater and filter water naturally.How a small land deal became a 3,950-acre conservation projectThe Conservation Law Center worked with the landowner and a local realtor to take the 191-acre parcel off the market while a longer-term solution was explored. The Conservation Fund stepped in with immediate financial support, purchasing the property with the intention of eventually transferring it into public ownership.That initial intervention created an opportunity to negotiate for the entire 3,950-acre holding rather than protecting just the smaller parcel. The Conservation Fund and the Southern Indiana Sentinel Landscape worked with American Land Holdings to secure the larger property, helping prevent the landscape from being divided into smaller privately owned plots.The project eventually brought together several organisations and public agencies. Funding support came from the US Navy through the Department of Defense's Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration programme, the US Fish and Wildlife Service's Pittman-Robertson Wildlife Restoration Program, The Nature Conservancy, the State of Indiana and the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation through Walmart's Acres for America programme.After more than two years of negotiations and fundraising, the Indiana Department of Natural Resources completed the acquisition in December 2024. The 3,950 acres, valued at more than $12 million, were permanently protected and established as the Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area. The acquisition was also reported by Indiana Public Media and The Indianapolis Star.Why protecting this landscape mattersThe property's location makes it valuable for more than its size. It sits in a transition zone between the western tallgrass prairie and the central hardwood forest, supporting a range of habitats that are increasingly important for wildlife. Its wetlands help absorb excess rainwater, reduce flooding and filter water, while the wooded and grassland sections provide shelter and feeding grounds for different species. The area also supports wildlife such as deer, wild turkey and migratory waterfowl.There is another reason the conservation project attracted federal support. The property lies close to the US Navy's Lake Glendora Test Facility, which is part of Naval Weapons Support Center Crane. Protecting compatible land uses around military installations helps preserve the surrounding environment while ensuring that nearby development does not interfere with military operations. This is one of the central ideas behind the Southern Indiana Sentinel Landscape initiative.A new public space for outdoor recreationThe property opened as Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area in April 2025, giving residents and visitors access to land that had previously been unavailable to the public for several years. Managed by the Indiana DNR's Division of Fish and Wildlife, the 3,950-acre area now offers opportunities for hunting, fishing, wildlife watching, hiking, foraging, trapping and other outdoor activities. Visitors can also explore its waterways using small boats, canoes and kayaks, while birdwatchers can observe migratory waterfowl gathering around its wetlands.The area does not have established hiking trails, but visitors can use available roadways and game trails to explore the property. The project also highlights how conservation efforts can depend on quick decisions and partnerships between organisations that bring different resources to the table. What initially appeared to be a relatively small land purchase became an opportunity to protect an entire ecological landscape.For Indiana, the result is not simply another addition to its public land network. It is the preservation of a former mining landscape that has developed into an important natural habitat, while ensuring that its wetlands, wildlife and recreational opportunities remain available to future generations.You use AI every day. articles.summary: An innovative idea to turn damaged cooking pots into seawater barriers is providing families in Gaza with some relief.
articles.body:
Khan Younis, Gaza – A few metres from the sea, near al-Qarara port on Gaza’s coast, Anas al-Shami, 33, is trying to keep his family of six warm and dry in a dilapidated tent. It offers little protection from wind and rain, while the damp seeps into their bedding and belongings at every moment. The swelling waves in the sea also pose a constant threat as winter approaches.

The beach was not al-Shami’s choice of place to live, but the refuge his family took shelter in after being displaced from their home quickly became overcrowded. They can’t afford anything safer than this tent.

Now, he and his family are living in constant fear of a repeat of last winter’s flooding.

Al-Shami and his family were forced to leave Bani Suheila, east of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, when it became part of Israel’s so-called “Yellow Zone” beyond which Palestinians are not permitted to go.

“I searched for land in displacement areas where I could pitch a tent, but overcrowding and high rental costs made that impossible,” he tells Al Jazeera. “I was therefore forced to stay on the beach, despite the dangers facing my family and me.”

Al-Shami recalls last winter, when seawater and rain flooded his tent while the family was asleep. He would wake to find his children lying in water. Their bedding and belongings were repeatedly soaked, leaving him unable to protect them from the cold as the tent turned into a pond.

Despite trying all year, the family has been unable to find anywhere else to go, leaving them facing another winter on the beach.

“My children’s repeated exposure to water, cold and damp caused serious illness which threatened their lives,” he says.

‘I feel helpless in front of my children’

It’s a familiar story along this stretch of coastline.

Ibrahim Abu Tair, 47, whose family has also been displaced from eastern Khan Younis, is sharing a cramped tent with his seven children on the port’s shoreline. The dilapidated shelter lacks any basic necessities and offers little protection from the cold, rain and wind.

“What hurts me most is feeling helpless in front of my children,” he says. “I cannot provide winter clothes to protect them from the cold or even a dry mattress for them to sleep on.”

The strong wind and the sound of the rising waves keep him awake at night, he says, and he is terrified of another flood like last year’s, when water inundated the tent and forced the family to endure the cold in the open. His greatest wish is to find safe shelter where his children can sleep without fear.

Some families have found a makeshift solution to keep the water at bay.

By filling damaged cooking pots with earth, they have forged a barrier against encroaching seawater alongside the tents.

Mayasem Association, an aid organisation which works in cooperation with World Central Kitchen, has seized on this innovation and is now producing these pot-barriers for families in this area close to al-Qarara port.

The initiative reuses large pots rendered unusable by repeated exposure to flames, corrosion and holes. Three pots, donated by World Central Kitchen, are filled with soil and stacked on top of one another, reaching approximately 150 centimetres in height to form barriers that hold back the incoming water and prevent waves from reaching shelter sites.

“The initiative initially involved building barriers to protect the association’s safe space, which hosts its education programmes, school, cultural activities, arts and heritage programmes,” Khalil Abu Lahia, the association’s emergency response coordinator, tells Al Jazeera. “The idea later developed into an attempt to protect the displaced families’ tents along the coastal strip.”

While this is an example of the innovative thinking which can help families who are destitute and at risk in Gaza, it is nevertheless only a temporary measure which cannot make up for the widespread lack of safe shelter.

The initiative comes amid a warning from Gaza’s Winter Emergency Committee of a worsening humanitarian catastrophe, as tents and caravans remain in critically short supply as Israeli authorities continue to prevent their entry into the Gaza Strip, alongside the delivery of critical construction materials and fuel.

The committee has reported that Israeli forces have also destroyed about 70 percent of municipalities’ essential operational equipment and 90 percent of civil defence rescue equipment. The fuel crisis means machinery and generators will soon stop functioning altogether, further limiting the ability to respond to floods, carry out rescue operations and clear roads.

In all, there are about 200,000 dilapidated tents sheltering hundreds of thousands of displaced people, including children, women and people with disabilities.

Some 7,800 of them are located in extremely hazardous areas, the committee has warned, including on dry riverbeds which may now flood, rainwater collection ponds and beaches exposed to crashing winter waves. These need to be urgently relocated to safer locations.

About 2,000 cracked buildings are also at risk of collapse, threatening families who have sought refuge inside them. Building materials, caravans, shelter and fuel are all urgently needed, the committee says.

articles.title: Serbian officers arrested for using ‘excessive force’ against protesters
articles.summary: Ten suspects are accused of abusing and torturing several people in the garage of a government compound in Belgrade.
articles.body:
Nine active Serbian police officers and one former officer have been arrested over accusations of using excessive force against students last year during protests that culminated in October’s electoral defeat of former President Aleksandar Vucic .

The Serbian Ministry of Interior announced Wednesday’s arrests, alleging that the suspects abused and tortured several people in the garage of a government compound in Belgrade in August 2025.

In a statement, the ministry said the suspects were on duty when they “used force and threats to inflict severe pain and suffering on several injured people, in order to obtain information, intimidate and unlawfully punish them”.

Anticorruption protests began in Serbia after 16 people were killed when the canopy at a railway station in Novi Sad collapsed in November 2024. The collapse was seen as symptomatic of alleged widespread corruption under Vucic, who served as president for 12 years before conceding defeat last month after parliamentary elections.

The ministry has released only the initials of the suspects but said they served in an elite unit. According to state broadcaster Radio Television of Serbia, the commander of the Special Antiterrorism Unit, Igor Zmiric, was among the detainees.

Since last month’s vote, the winning student-led protest movement has demanded reforms within state institutions, including the police and intelligence services. Protesters have also called on top officials to resign, accusing them of colluding with Vucic while he was in power.

Hopes that Belgrade would join the European Union have increased since October’s elections as the bloc offered to hold further accession talks if Serbia’s new government strengthens democracy.

In a 2025 report on Serbia, Amnesty International warned that protesters, journalists and civil society organisations “continued to face intimidation, harassment and unlawful surveillance as authorities sought to rein in widespread discontent”.

The rights group said protesters were subjected to excessive force in “multiple cases across the country”.

articles.title: Welsh aviation firm AerFin bought in £475m deal
articles.summary: The company, which was majority owned by a private equity firm, said it was beginning a "new chapter".
articles.body:
A Newport aviation company, that has grown into a global supplier of aircraft engines, parts and maintenance services, has been bought in a deal worth about £475m.

Japanese firm ORIX Aviation has agreed to acquire AerFin, which employs more than 230 people and operates from sites in the UK and around the world.

Founded by Bob James, AerFin has developed from a south Wales business into a global aviation aftermarket specialist.

Announcing the takeover, AerFin described it as the start of a new chapter for the company.

The firm - which was majority owned by a private equity company prior to the sale - buys, sells, leases and repairs aircraft, engines and components.

In 2025, the company moved into a new purpose-built, 116,000 sq ft facility at Indurent Park in Newport.

There are no plans to move its headquarters from Newport.

ORIX Aviation is the aircraft leasing arm of Japanese financial services giant the ORIX Group.

Chief executive Simon Goodson called the acquisition a "defining moment" in the company's history.

"I am delighted that AerFin is joining the ORIX Group, a business that shares our values and belief in trusted partnerships, flexible solutions and finding the way ahead for our customers," he said.

He said support from the wider ORIX Group would provide "the confidence and platform" to grow the aviation business.

"This is a defining moment in AerFin's story and the beginning of an exciting new chapter," said Goodson.

AerFin has built its existing business around extending the life of aircraft and engines through trading, leasing, repair and reuse.

It helps airlines and aviation companies source parts and manage assets. The company claims to serve more than 600 organisations.

For ORIX Aviation, the acquisition expands its activities beyond aircraft ownership and leasing, into aftermarket services and end-of-life aircraft management.

The company said the combination would strengthen its capabilities across the entire lifecycle of an aircraft.

James Meyler, chief executive of ORIX Aviation, said AerFin had built "a leading aviation aftermarket platform" supported by extensive technical expertise and an international customer base.

The sale also marks the exit of Danish private equity investor CataCap, which had been the majority shareholder in AerFin.

Founder Bob James said he was pleased to see the business move to what he described as "a long-term home", capable of supporting AerFin's next phase of expansion.

"I recognise a strong leadership team and a long-term home when I see one," James said.

articles.title: Six dead and others injured in fire at Brooklyn building
articles.summary: The cause of the blaze is not yet clear, after 230 fire and emergency medical personnel went to the scene.
articles.body:
Six people have died after a large fire broke out in a residential building in Brooklyn, New York City, officials say.

Several others were hurt in the blaze, which occurred early on Thursday morning, the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) said in a statement.

More than 230 fire and emergency medical personnel were sent to the scene near Sunset Park after the fire was first reported at around 01:40 local time (06:40 GMT).

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was "heartbroken" by the deaths, and has asked New Yorkers to "take a moment to pray for the full recovery of those who were injured".

The cause of the blaze is being investigated.

A crew specialising in hazardous materials was sent to the scene because of the presence of a lithium-ion battery, although it was not clear whether this was linked to the blaze.

The emergency responders reportedly discovered on their arrival that the building's first and second floors had been engulfed by flames.

Four individuals were pronounced dead at the scene, according to the FDNY.

A male and female were also taken to the hospital, where they were pronounced dead, the New York City Police Department (NYPD) said.

Six other civilians were injured, two of them critically, along with three firefighters, the FDNY said.

articles.title: Two Michigan neighbours agreed to split the cost of removing trees that threatened a barn, but the work never happened; after a $2,000 dispute, an appeals court ruled the homeowner could not sue over the same trees
articles.summary: A disagreement between two neighbours in Michigan over trees that threatened a barn has ended with an appeals court ruling against the homeowner who
articles.body: A disagreement between two neighbours in Michigan over trees that threatened a barn has ended with an appeals court ruling against the homeowner who wanted them removed. Seth Merle and Richard Hagopian had agreed to pay $2,000 each to remove the trees, but the work never happened. After a dispute over the money reached court, Merle filed another lawsuit over the same trees. On September 23, the Michigan Court of Appeals ruled that he could not bring the case again because the issue had already been decided.According to the judgment, the dispute involved two neighbouring properties in Livingston County, Michigan. Merle had a barn at the back of his property, close to land owned by Hagopian. Several trees stood on Hagopian's side of the boundary, and some of their branches extended onto Merle's property.Merle was worried that the trees might fall onto his barn and cause damage. He hired an expert to examine them, and the expert warned that some of the trees could fall onto his property within a year. This added to Merle's concerns about leaving them standing.The two neighbours initially agreed to share the cost of removing the trees. They signed a written agreement under which Merle would arrange the work and both men would contribute $2,000. They also agreed that if the work could not be completed, Merle would return Hagopian's money. However, the trees were not removed, and Hagopian did not get his money back and it soon became a court dispute.Neighbour demands his $2,000 backWhen the tree removal did not take place, Hagopian approached a small claims court to recover the money he had paid. Merle responded that Hagopian had failed to take proper care of the trees and that this had caused him damages.The judge ruled in Hagopian's favour and ordered Merle to return the $2,000, along with court costs. The court also rejected Merle's claim that Hagopian had been negligent in maintaining the trees.In its ruling, the court said the dispute concerning the trees on Hagopian's property had been fully resolved. It also stated that if any of those trees later fell and damaged Merle's property, Merle would be responsible for the damage.Homeowner files another lawsuit Merle filed a new case, again raising concerns about the trees growing on Hagopian's land. He argued that the trees were dangerous and that his neighbour had failed to maintain them properly. He also complained about branches extending onto his property and asked the court to take action.Hagopian argued that the earlier court had already dealt with the dispute and that Merle should not be allowed to bring another case over the same issue.Merle said the earlier case had mainly concerned the return of Hagopian's $2,000 and that the danger posed by the trees had not been properly considered.However, the second court pointed out that Merle himself had raised the issue of poor tree maintenance during the first case. His earlier complaint had accused Hagopian of negligence, meaning that the question of whether Hagopian was responsible for the condition of the trees had already been considered.The court also criticised Merle's tone when discussing the earlier judgment and rejected his attempt to reopen the dispute. Merle then challenged this decision before the Michigan Court of Appeals.What Appeals court saidThe appeals court examined whether Merle could file another lawsuit when a previous court had already considered his complaint about the trees.Merle argued that the problem was continuing because Hagopian had still not taken care of the trees. According to him, every day that the trees remained unattended was another day his neighbour had failed to address the danger.However, the appeals court did not agree. The judges explained that the earlier court had already considered whether Hagopian was negligent in maintaining the trees and had rejected Merle's claim.They found that Merle's new lawsuit concerned the same alleged failure to maintain the trees. Simply because the trees remained standing did not mean he could bring another case over the same complaint.The court also explained that once a dispute has been decided, the same parties generally cannot keep returning to court with claims arising from the same issue.You use AI every day.
